prophet: The Prophet ﷺ taught his friend Uqbah this surah and An-Nas and said: 'Read them every time you go to sleep and every time you get up.' (Abu Dawud and An-Nasa'i.)

The Prophet ﷺ asked a man, 'Should I tell you the best thing people use to ask for safety?' Then he said it was 'Say: I seek safety with the Lord of Al-Falaq' and 'Say: I seek safety with the Lord of the people.' (An-Nasa'i.)
Aisha said that when the Prophet ﷺ was sick, he read these two surahs over himself and blew. When his pain got worse, Aisha read them and wiped his hand over him. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Malik.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says Jabir, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and many others said Al-Falaq is the morning. It is like where Allah says He splits the daybreak.
The book Al-Jalalayn says Al-Falaq means the morning.
Ibn Kathir says this means from every bad thing in everything Allah made. Al-Hasan al-Basri said it means things like Hell and Iblis.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says it means any one of Allah's creations that has evil in it.

prophet: Aisha said the Prophet ﷺ took her hand, showed her the moon when it came up, and said: 'Ask Allah for safety from the bad of this when it goes dark.' (Ahmad and At-Tirmidhi.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says 'ghasiq' means night when it comes with darkness. Mujahid said 'when it waqab' means when the sun goes down.
Ibn Kathir also tells that some scholars said it means a star, or the moon.

prophet: Aisha said the Prophet ﷺ was once put under a magic spell. Two angels in a dream told him a man named Labid had done it, with a comb and hair, and it was hidden in a well. The Prophet ﷺ went and took it out. Aisha asked if he would tell everyone, and he said: 'Allah healed me, and I do not like to spread evil to people.' (Sahih al-Bukhari.)

Jibril once said to the Prophet ﷺ: 'In the name of Allah I read over you, from everything that hurts you, from the evil of every envious person and evil eye. May Allah heal you.' (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said this means women who do magic and blow on knots.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says this means magic that hurts.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says this is about Labid ibn al-A'sam, who was jealous of the Prophet ﷺ.
The book Al-Jalalayn says envy is when someone shows they are jealous of a good thing you have and acts on it.
